answers.answer: To list commands in a help reply, use {bot.commands.list.forUser}. It shows only the commands the person who started the reply may use. For bot information, use the first table: {bot.name}, {bot.mention}, {bot.isMod}, {bot.version}, {bot.license} and {bot.sourceCode}. No bot helper takes an argument after a colon.
answers.quote: For a help command, use {bot.commands.list.forUser}, so each viewer sees what they can run:

answers.answer: You must know that the helpers work only in bot-written text: commands, event responses, timers, pipelines, Discord notifications and webhooks. They do not work in text a viewer writes. You must also know that no bot helper takes an input after a colon. Both facts are in the first two paragraphs.
answers.quote: None of the bot helpers take an input after a colon.

answers.answer: {bot.name} is the bot name the install has on record. It is never the channel name, and it can differ from the account that posts the reply. A help reply works when the person who typed it sees only the commands that their role allows. When no bot name is on record, the reply shows NomNomzBot.
answers.quote: That name does not depend on the channel, so it is not your channel name.

answers.answer: Write the help reply as 'Commands for you: {bot.commands.list.forUser}'. Do not use {bot.name} to name the channel, because it is the install's bot name. If the reply must name the account that posts it, type that name by hand. A listed command can still be on cooldown. In a timer or an event response, the list shows only the commands everyone may use.
answers.quote: If the reply must name the account that posts it, type that name into the reply instead.

answers.answer: The page names two accounts: the shared bot and the bot that speaks in your chat. Then {bot.name} is described a third way, as the name the install has on record, and the page never says if that is the shared bot. I reread this. The rest of the page tells me what to do anyway, so it costs only a reread. I learned about the cooldown only after the help example, but it does not change what I write.
answers.quote: Two accounts matter on this page.

answers.answer: Read aloud, the helper {bot.lastRestart.relative} says 'restart', but the text says 'started'. A listener can think these are two different moments. The cost is small, because the section opens by saying a restart sets the count back to zero. The long dotted helper names are hard to hear, but they must be exact.
answers.quote: How long ago the bot started, rounded to the nearest day, hour or minute

warning_review.reason: The paragraph is dense, but each sentence answers a question the reader has about the bot name: what it is, why it is not the channel name, what shows when no name is set, and the older form. Answers 3 and 4 came from it without a reread. The one soft cost is the third-way wording in answer 5. It costs a reread, not a wrong action, so it stays.

The paragraph gives the three states of the moderator helper: true for your own account, false when not a moderator, and empty before the first check. The reader needs the empty state right after connecting their own bot. Each sentence adds one fact the reader would otherwise get wrong.
